title: Fresh Ginger Ale with Lime and Honey Syrup
summary: Sliced fresh ginger is simmered with water, sugar, honey and salt, lime juice is added, and the strained syrup is topped with cold soda water over ice.

ingredients.item: fresh ginger, sliced 5 mm thick (no need to peel)
fine sea salt or table salt
soda water or plain seltzer, very cold

steps.title: Simmer the ginger
steps.text: Put the ginger, water, sugar, honey and salt in the saucepan and bring to a simmer over medium heat. Lower the heat and cook gently for 15 minutes, stirring now and then, until it smells strongly of ginger.

steps.title: Add lime and cool
steps.text: Take the pan off the heat, stir in the lime juice and leave to cool completely, about 30 minutes.

steps.title: Strain
steps.text: Pour through the lined sieve into the bowl, pressing on the ginger to extract every drop, then discard the ginger. You will have about 360 ml syrup; pour it into the jar and chill.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Fill each glass with ice, add 60 ml syrup and top with about 180 ml cold soda water. Stir once, gently, and add a lime wedge.

tips: Young ginger is milder; mature, fibrous ginger gives more heat.
For a spicier ale, add a few slices of fresh ginger to the glass.
Stir gently after adding the soda water, or the bubbles escape.
Keep the soda water very cold; warm soda loses its fizz fast.
storage: The syrup keeps in a closed jar in the fridge for up to 1 week. Add the soda water only when serving. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
